To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mesenteric vessels from L-NAME hypertensives show an enhanced response in the presence of vasopressors, which is related to an increased calcium entry.

chronic NO deficiency leads to an increased response of the mesenteric vasculature to vasopressor agents and that this effect is related to an increased sensitivity to calcium entry and to a compensatory increase in the activity of a NO-independent vasodilating system.

the mesenteric arteries of the L- NAME hypertensive rats exhibit enhanced pressor responses to vasopressor agents and a reduced vasodilator response to acetylcholin, and that these responses are associated with an enhanced role of calcium entry and of a NO and a prostaglandin- independent vasodilator mechanism, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms involved in the development of hypertension in rats treated chronically with L-NAME.
the study of the mechanisms of increased mesenteric vascular responsiveness to vasopressor agents in the L- NAME hypertensive rats.
the mechanisms involved in the increased pressor responses of the mesenteric vascular bed of hypertensive rats with chronic inhibition of NO.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mesenteric vasculature from the L-NAME hypertensives is more responsive to vasopressor stimuli, but also to vasodilator stimuli.
the mesenteric vasculature of L-NAME rats is characterized by an increased sensitivity to vasoconstriction that is mediated through an enhanced calcium entry.

the increased pressor responses to vasoconstrictors in mesenteric arteries from L-NAME hypertensives are due to the increased calcium influx and to a compensatory increased release of endothelium-dependent hyperpolarizing factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

chronic L-NAME treatment induces a state of vascular hypertrophy, endothelial dysfunction and increased vascular reactivity in mesenteric vessels, which is associated with increased calcium sensitivity.
chronic NO deficiency induces mesenteric vascular hyperreactivity to vasopressor stimuli, which is related to increased calcium influx.

the mesenteric vasculature of NO-deficient hypertensive animals is characterized by an increase in vasoconstrictor responsiveness, which is related to the increased calcium sensitivity of the contractile elements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NO deficiency is associated with a significant increase in calcium influx in the vasculature.
the vasopressor response to methoxamine is enhanced in the mesenterics of L-NAME-treated hypertensive rats.
the mesenteric vasculature of hypertensive rats has an enhanced response to pressors, which is related to increased calcium entry.
